tldr: This paper studies score function estimation via empirical risk minimization with Sobolev ball constraints, achieving minimax rates for density estimation and score-based generative modeling.
motivation: Score functions are central to generative modeling, but their estimation suffers from overfitting; the authors aim to provide a principled regularization approach.
method: They constrain the hypothesis space to a Sobolev ball and derive minimax estimation rates for score functions on the flat torus, then extend the analysis to score-based generative models under a conjecture linking estimation rates to sample quality.
result: Minimax optimal rates are obtained for score function estimation under Sobolev constraints, and analogous rates are conjectured for generative modeling.
conclusion: Regularization via Sobolev balls is sufficient to achieve optimal estimation rates for score functions, with potential implications for score-based generative models.

title: Classical Freeness Of $\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_n$ At Level $1$ Via Combinatorics
authors: Shashank Kanade
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19234v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We use a family of Rogers--Ramanujan-type combinatorial identities of Dousse--Konan involving coloured partitions to prove classical freeness of the simple vertex operator algebras based on [MATH] at level [MATH]. These identities are used to produce Gr\"obner bases for the relevant arc algebras.
tldr: This paper uses combinatorial identities to prove classical freeness of certain vertex operator algebras.
motivation: To establish algebraic properties of vertex operator algebras via combinatorial methods.
method: Applies Rogers-Ramanujan-type identities and constructs Gröbner bases for arc algebras.
result: Proves classical freeness of simple vertex operator algebras based on sl_n at level 1.
conclusion: The combinatorial approach successfully verifies freeness, contributing to representation theory.

title: A Physical Adaptive Material Motor Unit Neural Network: A Hygromorph Composite Material Machine
authors: Charles de Kergariou, David Correa, Adam W. Perriman, Helmut Hauser, Fabrizio Scarpa
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18275v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Advances in novel materials science enable structures to function as intelligent machines by embedding memory and learning capabilities directly into materials. Our work introduces a physical adaptive material motor unit neural network,leveraging a new generation of controllable actuators composed of wood- and carbon black-based composites, sensitive to temperature and relative humidity. These material actuators are assembled into a motor unit-like structure inspired by muscle contraction trigger, forming an intelligent machine capable of dynamic shading control that can be used, for example, in buildings. The machine is governed by a neural network trained on over 350 experimental data points collected under diverse environmental conditions. By establishing a new data-aware backpropagation training, we show that the machine predicts shading responses and learns to predict appropriate behaviour incrementally as the database expands. We also demonstrate the ability of the machine to optimise configurations to achieve similar shading outputs under two distinct conditions.
tldr: A physical neural network made from hygromorph composite actuators for adaptive shading control.
motivation: To create intelligent machines by embedding memory and learning directly into materials, using environmentally responsive composites.
method: Wood- and carbon black-based composite actuators are assembled into motor units; a neural network is trained on experimental data using a data-aware backpropagation algorithm.
result: The machine predicts shading responses and learns incrementally as the database expands, optimizing configurations for similar outputs under different conditions.
conclusion: The approach demonstrates a novel material-based adaptive system for applications like dynamic building shading.

title: When Mobile Crowdsourcing Meets Queueing Systems: Human-in-the-Loop Learning
authors: Hongbo Li, Lingjie Duan, Ness B. Shroff
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18392v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In service systems, customers now rely on congestion information before deciding which queue or server to join, from restaurants and theme-park attractions to road networks. We study this setting as human-in-the-loop learning (HILL), where customers both consume and generate time-sensitive congestion information through crowdsourcing platforms. Because congestion reports become stale, efficient system operation requires continued exploration of servers whose current states are uncertain. Yet selfish customers avoid such exploration when it reduces their immediate service utility, even though their observations would benefit future customers. We analyze this tension between individual incentives and system-wide learning in queueing systems with endogenous congestion. We first show that myopic server choices can induce an infinite price of anarchy (PoA): decentralized customers may cause arbitrarily large efficiency losses by overexploring servers that are likely congested. In the single-server case, we prove that the lower bound on PoA decreases as buffer size grows, while in the multi-server case the upper bound decreases as the number of servers increases. We further show that existing informational, non-monetary mechanisms for exploration-exploitation with exogenous information fail in our setting, as customers' choices directly reshape the queue states and still lead to infinite PoA. To address this challenge, we design a dynamic side-payment mechanism that periodically charges some customers and rewards others, discouraging excessive exploration while maintaining ex-post budget balance. The mechanism coordinates congestion management and information acquisition across heterogeneous servers, and guarantees PoA below 2. Beyond worst-case analysis, experiments using real datasets demonstrate that the proposed mechanism also achieves strong average-case performance.
tldr: This paper studies human-in-the-loop learning in queueing systems with crowdsourced congestion information, focusing on the tension between individual incentives and system-wide learning.
motivation: Customers use crowdsourced congestion information to choose queues, but selfish behavior can lead to inefficient system operation due to under-exploration of uncertain servers.
method: The authors model the problem as a queueing system with endogenous congestion, analyze the price of anarchy (PoA) for myopic server choices, and propose a dynamic side-payment mechanism to coordinate exploration and exploitation.
result: Myopic choices can cause infinite PoA; the proposed side-payment mechanism guarantees PoA below 2 and achieves strong average-case performance on real datasets.
conclusion: Informational mechanisms fail in this setting, but a budget-balanced side-payment mechanism can effectively balance exploration and exploitation in queueing systems.

title: Evaluating The Effectiveness Of LLMs In Aiding Compliance Testing Of PKCS#1-v1.5
authors: Endadul Hoque Polina Kozyreva
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18405v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Testing implementations of binary protocols for specification compliance requires inputs that satisfy both structural and semantic constraints. Purely random generation and primitive mutations are often insufficient for exploring semantically meaningful behaviors in protocols that rely on Type-Length-Value (TLV) encoding, yet domain-specific compliance testing tools require deep protocol expertise and significant manual effort to construct. This work investigates whether grammar-level mutation combined with LLM-based code synthesis can serve as a viable, more generalizable approach to specification compliance testing. We evaluate the approach on PKCS#1 v1.5 signature verification -- a widely deployed TLV-encoded standard with a formally verified testing oracle (Morpheus) -- across 48 cryptographic library implementations. We reproduced 10 of 13 non-trivial specification violation categories previously identified by Morpheus, including all 5 signature forgery categories, and discovered 1 previously unreported discrepancy. We found that LLM hallucination -- occurring in 82.5% of generated scripts -- is the primary factor limiting effectiveness, not the mutation strategies. We identify five distinct hallucination types and show that their distribution varies systematically across mutation categories: structural mutations are implemented with 13.3% fidelity while constraint mutations achieve 30.3% correctness but suffer the highest rate of mutations being fully ignored (8.1%). These findings reveal a striking gap between operational reliability (99.8%) and semantic fidelity (17.5%), providing actionable guidance on when LLM-based code synthesis can be trusted in specification-driven testing pipelines.
tldr: This paper evaluates LLM-based code synthesis for compliance testing of PKCS#1 v1.5 signature verification, finding that LLM hallucination severely limits effectiveness.
motivation: Testing binary protocol implementations for specification compliance is challenging; existing tools require deep expertise and manual effort. The authors explore whether LLMs can automate this process.
method: They combine grammar-level mutation with LLM-based code synthesis to generate test inputs for PKCS#1 v1.5, and evaluate against 48 cryptographic libraries using a formally verified oracle (Morpheus).
result: They reproduced 10 of 13 known violation categories and discovered one new discrepancy. However, LLM hallucination occurred in 82.5% of generated scripts, with structural mutations achieving only 13.3% fidelity.
conclusion: LLM-based code synthesis for compliance testing is currently unreliable due to high hallucination rates; the approach requires significant improvement before practical deployment.

title: Ghost Vectors: Soft-Deleted Embeddings Remain Reconstructible In Hnsw Vector Databases
authors: Chandranil Chakraborttii, Jackeline Garc\'ia Alvarado, Sitora Abdulofizova, Shivanshu Dwivedi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18497v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) allows large language models to access external and private corpora for factual, domain-specific responses. Modern RAG pipelines use hierarchical navigable small world (HNSW) vector databases for efficient similarity search. When a user requests data deletion, the systems typically only mark the record as deleted, leaving the embedding on disk physically unchanged. This soft-delete operation raises compliance concerns under data-erasure and retention requirements such as GDPR Article 17 and HIPAA. Analysis on three HNSW implementations confirms that deleted vectors remain physically recoverable by accessing the raw index files at the storage layer, bypassing API access. Using the Vec2Text inversion model without domain-specific fine-tuning, we show this vulnerability on multiple real-world datasets and data modalities. On Wikipedia biographical living persons dataset (BLP), we successfully recover 25.5% of exact person names and 46.4% of geographic locations (ROUGE-L 0.185). Recovery reaches 100% for both patient age and gender markers (ROUGE-L 0.290) on highly structured, sensitive data (NIH Synthea dataset). On soft-deleted image embeddings, we show 100% tissue classification on histopathology patches (p=1.02e-07) and top-1 identity recovery reaches 99% on facial embeddings (p<0.01). This work introduces Epoch Key Rotation, which encrypts vectors and discards the key upon deletion. Epoch key rotation reduces observed PII recovery to 0% and completes in 2.5 ms for 500 deleted vectors (approximately 0.005 ms/record). Additionally, it generates an ECDSA-signed cryptographic proof as an auditable record of the deletion event.
tldr: This paper investigates the security vulnerability of soft-deleted embeddings in HNSW vector databases used for RAG, demonstrating that deleted vectors remain physically recoverable and proposing a cryptographic mitigation.
motivation: Soft-delete operations in vector databases may violate data erasure regulations like GDPR and HIPAA, as deleted embeddings remain on disk and can be reconstructed.
method: The authors analyze three HNSW implementations, use Vec2Text inversion to recover text from embeddings, and propose Epoch Key Rotation which encrypts vectors and discards the key upon deletion.
result: Recovery rates of up to 100% for sensitive attributes (e.g., age, gender) on structured data, and 99% identity recovery on facial embeddings; Epoch Key Rotation reduces PII recovery to 0% with low overhead.
conclusion: Soft-deleted embeddings in HNSW databases pose a privacy risk, but cryptographic key rotation can effectively mitigate the vulnerability.

title: Depth Lower Bounds For ReLU Networks With Binary Inputs
authors: Elchanan Mossel Neil Krishnan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18540v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the role of depth in ReLU networks with discrete (Boolean) inputs and real-valued outputs, complementing two established lines of work. For Boolean inputs, striking depth separation results were proven for [MATH] but with threshold ([MATH]) or ReLU gates depth separation is only established for depth two vs. three. On the other hand, for {\em real-valued} functions and ReLU networks, Telgarsky's (2016) constructed a simple one variable class of functions which establishes separation at higher depths. In this paper we are interested to establish an all-depths depth separation for ReLU networks on [MATH]. We do so by exhibiting an explicit family of functions computable exactly by a ReLU network of depth [MATH] and constant width, such that any ReLU network of depth [MATH] and width [MATH] computing the function exactly must satisfy [MATH]; in particular, no network of depth [MATH] can compute it with width polynomial in [MATH]. We note that our lower bound relies on computation as an exponential precision truncation of the output is computable by a polynomial-size [MATH] circuit.
tldr: Proves depth lower bounds for ReLU networks with binary inputs, showing exponential width is needed for shallow networks.
motivation: To understand the role of depth in neural networks for Boolean functions, complementing existing depth separation results.
method: Constructs an explicit family of functions computable by a deep ReLU network of depth d and constant width, then proves that any network of depth d-1 requires exponential width.
result: Any ReLU network of depth d-1 computing the function must have width at least exponential in d, while depth d networks can do it with constant width.
conclusion: Depth provides exponential savings in width for ReLU networks on Boolean inputs, establishing an all-depths separation.

title: Principal Component Analysis And Power Indices
authors: Xavier Molinero, Enric Mons\'o, Daniel Samaniego
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18559v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Measuring the influence of a player in a simple game is a widely studied topic. Shapley-Shubik power index is perhaps the maximum exponent in terms of relevance. Furthermore, other power indexes have been proposed over time. In this paper, we propose yet another power index, defined in terms of winning coalitions. We show that this index coincides with eigenvalues obtained with the Principal Component Analysis method, a broadly used technique in data science to determine the influence of different features given a dataset. Furthermore, we provide a characterization of this proposed index in terms of four properties.
tldr: This paper proposes a new power index for simple games based on principal component analysis and shows it coincides with eigenvalues.
motivation: Measuring influence in voting games is important; existing indices like Shapley-Shubik have limitations.
method: The authors define a power index using winning coalitions and prove it equals eigenvalues from PCA, then characterize it with four properties.
result: The proposed index is equivalent to PCA eigenvalues and satisfies a set of axiomatic properties.
conclusion: The new index offers a data-driven approach to measuring power in simple games.

title: Nanoscale Memristive Devices: Threats And Solutions
authors: Amir M. Hajisadeghi, Javad Talafy, Hamid R. Zarandi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18978v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Due to their incentivizing features, memristors are a promising candidate for replacing CMOS-based memories, which are faced with various functional challenges in deep submicron process technologies. Memristors are nonvolatile, have low leakage, and are dense in comparison to CMOS-based memories like SRAM. In this regard, resistive RAM (ReRAM) and spin-transfer-torque RAM (STT-RAM) memristors are distinguished among other memristor-based memory technologies, due to their superiority in process maturity and metrics such as memory operation energy, memory latency, and area. Hence, this chapter focuses on these two memristor-based memory technologies. Despite the good features of these types of memory, they suffer from some reliability threats. Reliability parameters affect each other, and examining their positive and negative effects has a significant impact on the effectiveness of the proposed solutions. In one view, the threats can be categorized into two classes: (1) read/write error and (2) soft error. In this chapter, we comprehensively describe these threats and present the state-of-the-art solutions that enable the widespread use of memristors, particularly ReRAM and STT-RAM, in different applications. Finally, we introduce the emerging ability of memristors as a computing unit aiming to minimize data restoration in computing, and we show how to perform logic and arithmetic computation in a crossbar array.
tldr: This paper reviews reliability threats and solutions for nanoscale memristive devices, focusing on ReRAM and STT-RAM, and introduces their use as computing units.
motivation: Memristors are promising for replacing CMOS memories but face reliability issues; the paper aims to comprehensively describe these threats and present state-of-the-art solutions.
method: The paper categorizes threats into read/write errors and soft errors, and surveys existing mitigation techniques; it also demonstrates logic and arithmetic computation in crossbar arrays.
result: The paper provides a taxonomy of reliability threats and a collection of solutions, and shows that memristors can perform computing tasks to minimize data restoration.
conclusion: Memristors, especially ReRAM and STT-RAM, have potential for memory and computing applications if reliability challenges are addressed.

title: Multi-network Comparison Of Between-farm Contacts For Infectious Disease Surveillance In Swine Production
authors: Jason A. Galvis, Nicolas C. Cardenas, Gustavo Machado
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18277v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding how swine farms are interconnected, directly and indirectly, is essential to characterizing infectious disease transmission. This study aimed to describe the connectivity of swine farms across 11 network types, including vehicle movements (i.e., trucks and trailers), animal movements, and distance-based farm-to-farm contacts, to identify links among production types and farms likely to be consistently characterized as super-spreaders. Truck and trailer movement networks were the most densely connected, particularly for feed transport, showing connectivity levels between 98.7% and 99.7% higher than those of pig movement and distance-based networks. These networks also exhibited the highest degree and frequency of connections between farms, while the aggregated truck network, which included all truck types, showed the greatest potential to act as a bridge connecting farms. Finisher farms were highly interconnected with other farm types across all networks. Sow farms were frequently reached by other farm types, especially through feed truck movements, representing up to 8.7% of these links. We demonstrated that in vehicle movements and proximity networks, finisher farms played a major role as super-spreaders. When comparing the top 50 farms ranked by super-spreader score in each network, vehicle-based networks showed the highest similarity, with up to 89% of top-ranked farms shared between vehicle networks. In contrast, pig movement and distance-based networks identified largely distinct sets of top-ranked farms, sharing at most 4% and 8%, respectively, with other contact networks. Overall, each network exhibited a distinct connectivity structure, resulting in different sets of high-risk farms, particularly regarding potential transmission to breeding farms. These findings support the integration of multiple transmission pathways into disease surveillance.
tldr: This paper analyzes swine farm connectivity across multiple network types to identify super-spreader farms for infectious disease surveillance.
motivation: Understanding how swine farms are interconnected is essential for characterizing infectious disease transmission and improving surveillance.
method: The study compares 11 network types including vehicle movements, animal movements, and distance-based contacts, using network analysis to identify connectivity patterns and super-spreader farms.
result: Vehicle movement networks (especially feed trucks) are the most densely connected, and finisher farms are major super-spreaders; different networks identify largely distinct sets of high-risk farms.
conclusion: Integrating multiple transmission pathways into disease surveillance is supported, as each network reveals different connectivity structures and high-risk farms.

title: Extension Of A Multi-region Free-surface Mhd Solver Beyond The Inductionless Approximation
authors: Min Ki Jung, Brian Wynne, Francisco Saenz, Yufan Xu, Jabir Al-Salami, Yong-Su Na, Egemen Kolemen
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18745v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Free-surface liquid metal flows are a leading candidate for the plasma-facing components of future fusion reactors. Existing transient, three-dimensional, free-surface MHD solvers rely on the inductionless approximation in which the induced magnetic field is neglected. This paper extends the open-source solver FreeMHD [B. Wynne et al., Phys. Plasmas 32, 013907 (2025)] beyond the inductionless approximation to resolve the induced magnetic field self-consistently using a vector-potential formulation that enforces [MATH] by construction while preserving the original multi-region, two-phase framework. The solver is verified against analytical Shercliff and Hunt duct-flow solutions across a range of Hartmann numbers and validated against free-surface height measurements from the LMX-U experiment. To the best of our knowledge, FreeMHD2 is the first open-source, experimentally validated free-surface liquid metal solver to resolve the evolution of the induced magnetic field without invoking the inductionless approximation. By removing this approximation rather than relaxing it, the formulation provides the basis for future modeling of the finite magnetic Reynolds number conditions expected in large-scale, transient fusion events.
tldr: This paper extends a free-surface MHD solver for liquid metal flows in fusion reactors beyond the inductionless approximation.
motivation: Existing free-surface MHD solvers neglect induced magnetic fields, limiting their accuracy for large-scale transient fusion events.
method: The solver uses a vector-potential formulation that enforces divergence-free magnetic field while preserving the multi-region, two-phase framework.
result: The solver is verified against analytical duct-flow solutions and validated with experimental free-surface height measurements from LMX-U.
conclusion: FreeMHD2 is the first open-source, experimentally validated free-surface liquid metal solver to resolve induced magnetic fields without the inductionless approximation.

title: Volumetric Nanoscale Localization Using Engineered Point Spread Functions In Light Sheet Microscopy
authors: R. E. Bautista Gonzalez, R. Mouthaan, A. Upadhya, D. J. X. Chow, K. R. Dunning, K. Dholakia
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18784v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nanoscale three-dimensional localization across large biological volumes remains an outstanding challenge in optical microscopy, with existing approaches typically limited by imaging speed, volumetric field of view and localization precision when required simultaneously. Here, we overcome these limitations by combining a twin Airy engineered point spread function with two-photon light sheet fluorescence microscopy, enabling nanoscale localization throughout large volumetric fields of view. Our framework explicitly incorporates the broadband fluorescence emission characteristic of biological fluorophores, ensuring accurate localization under realistic imaging conditions. We achieve localization precisions of [MATH]~nm laterally and 42~nm axially over volumes measuring 295~[MATH]m x 330~[MATH]m x 100~[MATH]m , with a projected path to sub-10-nm localization in millimeter-scale specimens. Experiments in fluorescent bead phantoms and live mammalian oocytes confirm robust performance in both controlled and biologically complex environments. These results establish a scalable strategy for localization-based super-resolution imaging across biologically relevant volumes, bridging the gap between nanoscale precision and large-scale volumetric microscopy.
tldr: This paper presents a method for nanoscale 3D localization in light sheet microscopy using engineered point spread functions.
motivation: Existing optical microscopy techniques struggle to achieve nanoscale precision across large biological volumes simultaneously.
method: The authors combine a twin Airy engineered point spread function with two-photon light sheet fluorescence microscopy, incorporating broadband fluorescence emission characteristics.
result: They achieve localization precisions of ~nm laterally and 42 nm axially over volumes of 295 µm x 330 µm x 100 µm, with a path to sub-10-nm in millimeter-scale specimens.
conclusion: This work establishes a scalable strategy for localization-based super-resolution imaging across biologically relevant volumes.

title: EDoF-NeRF: Extended Depth-of-field Neural Radiance Fields Using A Coded Aperture Camera
authors: Ryoichi Horisaki Yoshiyuki Shirasaki
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18826v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a method for extending the depth-of-field (DoF) to construct high-fidelity neural radiance fields (NeRF) -- an emerging technique for rendering photorealistic novel views from a dataset of images captured at different viewpoints, based on implicit neural representations. The trade-off between DoF and light quantity is inherent not only in conventional cameras but also in NeRF, since the datasets used by NeRF are captured by these cameras. To address this issue, we introduce a coded aperture placed at the camera pupil, preserving spatial frequency components under defocused conditions. We develop a camera model incorporating coded apertures into NeRF, allowing direct input of coded images and enabling the generation of novel views with an extended DoF. We validate the proposed method, termed extended DoF-NeRF (EDoF-NeRF), through simulations and experiments, demonstrating its superior performance compared to conventional aperture cameras.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to extend the depth-of-field in neural radiance fields using a coded aperture camera.
motivation: Neural radiance fields suffer from a trade-off between depth-of-field and light quantity due to conventional camera limitations. The authors aim to improve NeRF reconstruction quality by preserving spatial frequencies under defocus.
method: A coded aperture is placed at the camera pupil to modulate the incoming light, and a camera model incorporating coded apertures is integrated into the NeRF framework, allowing direct input of coded images.
result: Simulations and experiments demonstrate that the proposed EDoF-NeRF method outperforms conventional aperture cameras in extending depth-of-field while maintaining high-fidelity novel view synthesis.
conclusion: Coded apertures effectively mitigate the DoF-light trade-off in NeRF, enabling high-quality reconstruction from defocused images.

title: A Finite Element-based Eigenvalue Analysis For Predicting Thermal Runaway In Li-ion Battery Packs
authors: Shailendra Rahi (indian Institute Of Technology Ropar), Vinay Dhakal (university Of Texas At Arlington), Ankur Jain (university Of Texas At Arlington), Manish Agrawal
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18983v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Thermal runaway remains a critical safety concern in battery systems and other thermally active devices, necessitating reliable methods for predicting the conditions under which thermal runaway may occur. In this work, we develop a finite element framework for assessing thermal stability in systems undergoing transient heat conduction with temperature-dependent internal heat generation. The formulation leads naturally to a generalized eigenvalue problem, wherein the sign of the smallest eigenvalue provides a direct criterion for determining the onset of thermal runaway. This approach enables direct prediction of thermal runaway thresholds in geometrically complicated problems without requiring computationally expensive transient analysis. The proposed methodology is validated through comparison with analytical solutions for a cylindrical Li-ion cell, as well as with a pack of cylindrical cells, demonstrating excellent agreement in both cases. Based on this model, the influence of material properties, boundary conditions, geometric parameters, and spatially varying heat generation on stability limits is examined. A key advantage of this formulation is its effectiveness even for complex geometries where analytical methods become impractical. By providing a systematic and computationally efficient means to identify stability thresholds, the present work offers a practical tool for the thermal design and safety assessment of battery systems.
tldr: This paper uses finite element eigenvalue analysis to predict thermal runaway in Li-ion battery packs, focusing on thermal safety engineering.
motivation: Thermal runaway is a critical safety issue in battery systems; reliable prediction methods are needed.
method: A finite element framework is developed that reduces transient heat conduction with temperature-dependent heat generation to a generalized eigenvalue problem; the sign of the smallest eigenvalue indicates thermal runaway onset.
result: The method is validated against analytical solutions for cylindrical cells and battery packs, showing excellent agreement, and parametric studies reveal influences of material properties and geometry.
conclusion: The eigenvalue approach provides a computationally efficient tool for thermal stability assessment in complex battery geometries.

title: Extension Of Hypercyclic And Frequently Hypercyclic Subspaces
authors: Felipe Carvalho Silva, Geivison Ribeiro, R\'egis Var\~ao
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18252v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We focus on the existence of large linear structures within the sets of hypercyclic and frequently hypercyclic vectors. For operators [MATH] satisfying Kitai's Criterion or the Frequent Hypercyclicity Criterion, we analyze the fundamental linear space [MATH], studied by Herrero, Bourdon, B\`es, Wengenroth, and many others. We show that the set [MATH] can be extended within [MATH] or [MATH] if [MATH] or [MATH], respectively. The extension is such that the quotient of the new space with [MATH] has dimension [MATH] (the cardinality of the continuum). Second, we prove that generically a finite-dimensional subspace contained in [MATH] can be enlarged to a subspace of dimension [MATH]. Third, we establish sufficient conditions for extending arbitrary linear subspaces both from [MATH] and [MATH] to larger subspaces of dimension [MATH].
tldr: This paper studies hypercyclic and frequently hypercyclic subspaces in linear dynamics, a topic in functional analysis.
motivation: To understand the existence of large linear structures within sets of hypercyclic and frequently hypercyclic vectors for operators satisfying certain criteria.
method: The authors analyze the fundamental linear space studied by Herrero, Bourdon, Bès, Wengenroth, and others, and prove extension results using quotient space dimension arguments.
result: They show that the set can be extended within certain spaces to a subspace whose quotient with the original has dimension continuum, and that generically a finite-dimensional subspace can be enlarged to dimension continuum.
conclusion: The results provide sufficient conditions for extending arbitrary linear subspaces to larger subspaces of dimension continuum.

title: A Generalized Transform Framework For A Nonlinear Model Of Cancer Dynamics
authors: Gabriela Lopez, Hector Carmenate, Jyrko Correa-Morris
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18291v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops a generalized transform framework for a logistic--Allee tumor-growth model. The method combines a generalized Laplace transform, Adomian decomposition, Chebyshev--Pad\'e rational reconstruction, and a \(\mu\)-scaled generalized transform to obtain admissible semi-analytical approximations. Comparisons with experimental tumor-growth data show that the resulting compact representations are stable, admissible, and comparable in error to standard numerical reference solutions.
tldr: This paper develops a generalized transform framework for a logistic-Allee tumor-growth model, combining Laplace transforms, Adomian decomposition, and Chebyshev-Padé reconstruction to obtain semi-analytical approximations.
motivation: To improve analytical solutions for nonlinear cancer dynamics models, enabling better understanding and prediction of tumor growth.
method: Combines a generalized Laplace transform, Adomian decomposition, Chebyshev-Padé rational reconstruction, and a μ-scaled generalized transform to derive semi-analytical approximations.
result: The compact representations are stable, admissible, and comparable in error to standard numerical reference solutions when tested against experimental tumor-growth data.
conclusion: The proposed framework provides a viable semi-analytical approach for modeling cancer dynamics with nonlinear growth laws.

title: Starter-Iterator Neural Operator: A Unified Architecture For High-Fidelity Forward And Inverse Pde Problems
authors: Kuilin Qin, Lianfang Wang, Xu Sun, Jiwei Jia, Yu Wang, Yong Wang, Yuping Duan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18305v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Operator learning is an emerging interdisciplinary field that integrates machine learning with scientific computing. By mapping infinite-dimensional function spaces, this approach provides an efficient surrogate modeling framework for high-dimensional partial differential equations (PDEs). Compared to traditional numerical solvers, it achieves a superior trade-off between computational complexity and approximation accuracy, demonstrating significant advantages in many-query tasks such as real-time prediction and parameter sweeps. Given the stringent accuracy requirements of both forward simulation and inverse inference, as well as the precision bottlenecks of existing operator learning methods in handling complex boundaries or long-term evolution, we propose the Starter-Iterator Neural Operator (SINO). Our framework reinterprets the initialization strategies and iterative formats of traditional iterative methods through neural networks, establishing an efficient approach for spectral-spatiotemporal collaborative modeling. Specifically, the frequency-domain initialization module captures globally stable low-frequency features, while the time-domain learning module focuses on optimizing local solution residuals, thereby effectively overcoming the inherent limitations of conventional single-domain modeling approaches. Extensive experiments on typical dynamical systems such as the Navier-Stokes equations and acoustic wave equations, as well as practical applications including super-resolution imaging and weather forecasting, demonstrate that SINO achieves outstanding performance in numerical accuracy, generalization capability, and robustness.
tldr: This paper proposes a neural operator architecture for solving PDEs, combining frequency-domain and time-domain modules.
motivation: Existing operator learning methods struggle with complex boundaries and long-term evolution, limiting accuracy in forward and inverse PDE problems.
method: The Starter-Iterator Neural Operator (SINO) uses a frequency-domain initialization module for global low-frequency features and a time-domain learning module for local residual optimization.
result: SINO achieves high numerical accuracy, generalization, and robustness on Navier-Stokes, acoustic wave equations, super-resolution, and weather forecasting.
conclusion: The proposed architecture offers a unified and efficient surrogate modeling framework for high-fidelity PDE solutions.

title: Time And Frequency Domain Analysis Of Love Waves Generated By Gaussian, Ricker And Double Couple Seismic Sources In A Memory Dependent Fractured Poroviscoelastic Layer On A Heterogeneous Viscoelastic Half-space
authors: Anisha Kumari, Subhajyoti Sarkar, Santimoy Kundu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18359v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The present study develops a detailed theoretical and mathematical formulation to analyze the time and frequency domain propagation characteristics of Love waves in a stratified fractured poroviscoelastic continuum.The top stratum is modeled as a fractured poroviscoelastic material,whereas the lower semi infinite region exhibits heterogeneity and a gradual transition from viscoelastic behavior near the interface to purely elastic response at greater depths.Fractional order constitutive relations are incorporated to capture the memory-dependent mechanical behavior of the medium using Riemann Liouville fractional derivatives. Three distributed source models, namely Gaussian, Ricker and double-couple sources, are considered. To the best of our knowledge, the mathematical formulation of these distributed sources within the present framework has not been established in earlier studies, where the excitation is typically modeled using an idealized point source. By applying Fourier transform techniques in conjunction with Greens function methodology, the complex dispersion relation is obtained. Since the resulting dispersion equation yields complex roots, a hybrid Newton Raphson iterative algorithm is employedto compute these roots efficiently. Synthetic seismograms are generated to verify that the obtained solutions remain physically consistent and meaningful. Numerical simulations are then performed to investigate the effects of heterogeneity, fractional viscoelasticity and porosity on wave propagation characteristics, thereby identifying the parameters that exert the most significant influence on the system response. Furthermore, to examine the structural implications of the propagated waves, a single degree of freedom SDOF oscillator model is employed to evaluate the surface response corresponding to different types of seismic sources.
tldr: This paper studies Love wave propagation in a fractured poroviscoelastic layer on a heterogeneous viscoelastic half-space using Gaussian, Ricker, and double-couple seismic sources.
motivation: To develop a theoretical model for Love waves in complex geological media with memory-dependent behavior and distributed sources, which has not been done before.
method: Fractional order constitutive relations with Riemann-Liouville derivatives are used; Fourier transform and Green's function methods yield a complex dispersion relation solved via hybrid Newton-Raphson iteration.
result: Synthetic seismograms are generated and numerical simulations show the effects of heterogeneity, fractional viscoelasticity, and porosity on wave propagation.
conclusion: The model provides physically consistent results and identifies key parameters influencing the system response, with implications for structural response analysis.

title: Two-level Convergence Of Algebraic Multigrid With Overlapping Smoothers And Spectral Coarse Grids
authors: O. A. Krzysik, B. S. Southworth, H. Al Daas
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18404v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We recently developed the least-squares algebraic-multigrid domain-decomposition (LS-AMG-DD) solver as an algebraic multilevel method for sparse symmetric positive definite matrices that admit a Gram representation \(A=G^{\top}G\) . Many problem classes admit such structure, including many conforming finite-element discretizations. The solver constructs coarse spaces from local eigenproblems on nonoverlapping, algebraic aggregates and uses Schwarz-type smoothers on the induced overlapping subdomains. This paper develops a novel two-level convergence theory for this solver. Our theory shows that the solver's coarse space satisfies a weak approximation property in a norm induced by an aggregate-wise block-Jacobi smoother, and moreover, that the corresponding approximation constant is bounded by a user-controlled local spectral cutoff threshold. We combine this approximation property with standard sharp theory for multiplicative two-level cycles. The resulting two-level bound is cleanly factored by the cutoff threshold and a smoother norm-comparison constant; we derive explicit bounds for this constant for block Jacobi and overlapping additive Schwarz smoothers. We also develop a new convergence bound for additive Schwarz methods in terms of a trivially computable constant that is bounded above by the coloring constant. Numerical experiments on scalar \(H^1\), vector \(H()\), and vector \(H()\) finite-element problems provide supporting evidence for the theory, including evidence for the solver's insensitivity to mesh refinement and polynomial degree.
tldr: This paper develops a two-level convergence theory for an algebraic multigrid solver with overlapping smoothers and spectral coarse grids, applied to finite-element discretizations.
motivation: To provide rigorous convergence guarantees for the LS-AMG-DD solver, which is used for solving sparse symmetric positive definite systems arising from finite-element discretizations.
method: The authors derive a weak approximation property for the coarse space in a norm induced by an aggregate-wise block-Jacobi smoother, and combine it with standard multiplicative two-level cycle theory to obtain a two-level convergence bound.
result: The two-level bound is factored by a user-controlled spectral cutoff threshold and a smoother norm-comparison constant, with explicit bounds for block Jacobi and overlapping additive Schwarz smoothers.
conclusion: Numerical experiments on scalar and vector finite-element problems confirm the theory and show insensitivity to mesh refinement and polynomial degree.

title: Numerically Stable Cholesky-QR On Gpu Via Mixed-Precision Randomized Preconditioning
authors: James E. Garrison, Chao Chen, Ilse C. F. Ipsen
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18411v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cholesky-QR is among the fastest algorithms for computing the thin QR factorization of tall-and-skinny matrices on GPUs, relying entirely on BLAS-3 operations. However, it is numerically unstable: forming the Gram matrix squares the condition number, causing breakdown when [MATH]. We present MRCQR (Mixed-Precision Randomized Cholesky-QR), a stable GPU algorithm that addresses this limitation. MRCQR uses a subsampled randomized trigonometric transform to construct a preconditioner [MATH] that reduces [MATH] to near unity with high probability, then applies Cholesky-QR in double precision to the preconditioned matrix. The key insight -- supported by perturbation analysis -- is that the preconditioner requires far less accuracy than the final result: single (FP32) precision suffices when [MATH], and half (FP16) when [MATH]. MRCQR produces an explicit orthogonal factor [MATH] satisfying [MATH] ([MATH], double-precision unit roundoff) for condition numbers up to [MATH], far beyond the [MATH] limit of CholQR2. Experiments on an NVIDIA H100 GPU show that MRCQR (FP16) outperforms rand-cholQR by [MATH]--[MATH] across all tested column counts and is [MATH]--[MATH] faster than cuSOLVER geqrf, while the FP16 sketch (used when [MATH]) is [MATH] cheaper than FP64 at no accuracy cost.
tldr: This paper presents a numerically stable GPU algorithm for tall-and-skinny QR factorization using mixed-precision randomized preconditioning.
motivation: Cholesky-QR is fast on GPUs but numerically unstable for ill-conditioned matrices; the authors aim to extend its applicability to higher condition numbers.
method: The algorithm uses a subsampled randomized trigonometric transform to precondition the matrix in low precision (FP16/FP32), then applies Cholesky-QR in double precision.
result: MRCQR achieves stability for condition numbers up to 10^16, outperforms existing methods on H100 GPU, and reduces sketch cost by 2x with no accuracy loss.
conclusion: Mixed-precision randomized preconditioning effectively stabilizes Cholesky-QR, making it practical for large-scale tall-and-skinny matrices on GPUs.

title: The Ma\~n\'e-Freire Formula Holds For Magnetic Flows
authors: Anthony J. Garc\'ia Guilherme Brand\~ao Guglielmo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18434v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we use the recently introduced notation and terminology for magnetic systems, which provide a natural framework for extending techniques and results from the theory of geodesic flows to magnetic flows. In this context, we prove a magnetic analogue of the classical Freire--Ma\~n\'e theorem and obtain some applications. As a consequence, we show that for an energy level of a magnetic system without focal points, either the metric entropy is positive or the magnetic curvature is identically zero.
tldr: The paper proves a magnetic analogue of the Freire–Mañé theorem for magnetic flows, relating metric entropy to curvature.
motivation: Extend classical results from geodesic flows to magnetic flows using a new notation and terminology for magnetic systems.
method: Adapts techniques from geodesic flow theory to the magnetic setting, proving a magnetic version of the Freire–Mañé formula.
result: For an energy level of a magnetic system without focal points, either the metric entropy is positive or the magnetic curvature is identically zero.
conclusion: The magnetic analogue of the Freire–Mañé theorem holds, with applications to entropy and curvature.

title: Sequential Hiring Of Contingent Workers Through Learning-Based Optimization
authors: Chris Lee, Xiuli Chao, Izak Duenyas
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18438v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study a sequential workforce management problem in a contingent labor setting with uncertainty in both worker production and labor supply. A firm seeks to maximize cumulative profit by maintaining an active team of fixed size while learning worker productivity over time. We emphasize two critical operational frictions in this problem: replacing workers is costly, and workers may not be available immediately for hiring because of, for example, prior job commitments, scheduling constraints, or onboarding procedures. Thus, hiring decisions take effect only after a random delay. We formulate this problem as a stochastic multi-play bandit with costly switching and delayed actions, and develop a learning-based hiring policy, DR-UCB (DelayedReplacement-UCB), that makes replacement and hiring decisions sequentially through learning cycles. In each cycle, the policy uses real-time production data to determine when to initiate workforce changes and which workers to replace and hire. We show that the leading-order regret of the proposed policy matches its lower bound in its dependence on the time horizon. Our numerical experiments show that DR-UCB outperforms benchmark policies.
tldr: This paper studies a sequential workforce management problem using a multi-play bandit framework with costly switching and delayed hiring, focusing on operational optimization rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The firm aims to maximize cumulative profit by maintaining a fixed-size team while learning worker productivity, facing costly replacements and random hiring delays.
method: The problem is formulated as a stochastic multi-play bandit with costly switching and delayed actions, and a learning-based policy DR-UCB is developed that makes replacement and hiring decisions through learning cycles.
result: The policy achieves leading-order regret matching the lower bound in time horizon dependence, and numerical experiments show it outperforms benchmarks.
conclusion: The proposed DR-UCB policy effectively addresses the operational frictions of costly switching and delayed hiring in contingent workforce management.

title: Intermediate Bilevel Optimization: Modeling Endogenous Follower Tie-Breaking Behavior
authors: Maria Bazotte, Margarida Carvalho, Thibaut Vidal
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18475v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In bilevel optimization, optimistic and pessimistic follower behaviors are the most commonly used forms to define how the follower ties-breaks among multiple optimal solutions. In this work, we go beyond these extreme tie-breaking behaviors and investigate the intermediate bilevel optimization program (I-BO), where the follower's selected optimal response is a decision-dependent random event, with a probability measure influenced by the leader's decision. We formally introduce a class of such endogenous measures, including the special case of strong-weak decision-dependent I-BO. We reformulate the I-BO as a Transformed I-BO (T-I-BO) with exogenous uncertainty by defining inverse and Markov-chain transformations, which represent the follower's response as a function of the leader's decision and exogenous randomness. We handle the T-I-BO's uncertainty via sample-average approximation (SAA), and we propose tailored approaches for its SAA program according to the chosen transformation. Computationally, our methods solve reasonable-sized instances efficiently and outperform the deterministic equivalent when available. Furthermore, experiments stress the critical need to accurately model follower tie-breaking behavior, particularly depending on its alignment with the leader's objective, as misspecification leads to suboptimal leader decisions.
tldr: This paper introduces a bilevel optimization model where the follower's tie-breaking behavior is endogenous and decision-dependent, and proposes transformations to handle the uncertainty.
motivation: Standard optimistic/pessimistic tie-breaking assumptions in bilevel optimization may be unrealistic; this work aims to model intermediate behaviors where the follower's choice is probabilistic and influenced by the leader's decision.
method: The authors define a class of endogenous probability measures for follower tie-breaking, reformulate the problem via inverse and Markov-chain transformations to convert it into a problem with exogenous uncertainty, and solve the resulting sample-average approximation using tailored approaches.
result: The proposed methods solve reasonable-sized instances efficiently and outperform the deterministic equivalent when available; experiments show that misspecifying tie-breaking behavior leads to suboptimal leader decisions.
conclusion: Accurately modeling follower tie-breaking is critical in bilevel optimization, and the intermediate bilevel optimization framework provides a more flexible and realistic approach.

title: Conley Index Theory For Hybrid Systems
authors: William Kalies Bernardo Rivas
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18501v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We define a homological Conley index for a class of hybrid dynamical systems. This is achieved by factoring through the hybrid suspension semiflow, which views a class of hybrid dynamics as a continuous semiflow. We establish that this invariant is well-defined, invariant under continuation, and satisfies the Wa\.zewski property and other reconstruction results. We compute the index for several examples, showcasing how classical reconstruction theorems apply in this setting to characterize hybrid dynamics.
tldr: This paper develops a homological Conley index for hybrid dynamical systems, which is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Hybrid systems combine continuous and discrete dynamics, and the Conley index is a topological tool for studying invariant sets; the authors aim to extend this index to hybrid systems.
method: The authors factor hybrid dynamics through a hybrid suspension semiflow to define a homological Conley index, and prove its well-definedness, invariance under continuation, and the Ważewski property.
result: The index is computed for several examples, demonstrating how classical reconstruction theorems apply to characterize hybrid dynamics.
conclusion: The Conley index provides a useful invariant for analyzing hybrid dynamical systems, but the work has no connection to the user's research interests.

title: On Locally Distinguishing Sierpi\'nski Dynamical Systems
authors: Sergei Merenkov
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18505v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that there is no local quasiconformal map between the limit set of a convex-cocompact Kleinian group and the Julia set of a postcritically finite rational map, provided that both are Sierpi\'nski carpets. This contrasts with the recent results by Y. Luo, D. Ntalampekos and Y. Luo, M. Mj, S. Mukherjee for gasket and tree-like spaces, respectively.
tldr: Proves non-existence of local quasiconformal maps between certain Sierpiński carpet limit sets and Julia sets.
motivation: To understand when fractal sets arising from different dynamical systems can be locally equivalent.
method: Uses quasiconformal geometry and properties of Sierpiński carpets from Kleinian groups and rational maps.
result: No local quasiconformal map exists between such carpets, contrasting with known results for gasket and tree-like spaces.
conclusion: Sierpiński carpets from these two classes are locally distinct, highlighting rigidity in conformal dynamics.

title: Scalar-Tracking Sav Schemes With Pullback Corrections For Gradient Flows
authors: Jie Shen Shiheng Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18551v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The scalar auxiliary variable (SAV) method constructs linear, unconditionally energy-stable time discretizations of gradient flows. In a first-order SAV step, eliminating the auxiliary variable shows that the state equation is a semi-implicit update augmented by a rank-one positive semidefinite correction from the previous nonlinear force. The multiple-SAV (MSAV) method produces this correction componentwise, yielding a correction of rank up to the number of energy components. This separates two mechanisms usually coupled in MSAV: the number of scalar variables tracking the nonlinear energy and the rank of the correction applied to the state equation. We introduce a pullback-corrected SAV (PB-SAV) family that keeps a single scalar auxiliary variable but replaces the rank-one SAV correction by the pullback correction induced by an admissible component decomposition. The correction remains positive semidefinite, has rank at most the number of components, and may change from step to step without changing the scalar energy tracker. We prove modified-energy dissipation laws for fixed and step-dependent decompositions, derive a refinement identity whose gain is an explicit weighted variance, and give a Sherman-Morrison-Woodbury implementation of the low-rank perturbation of the standard semi-implicit solve. We also show, in finite dimensions, that the pullback correction is the Gauss-Newton matrix of a least-squares representation of the nonlinear energy. Numerical experiments on finite-dimensional gradient flows, Allen-Cahn dynamics, and nonlocal Cahn-Hilliard models illustrate regimes in which PB-SAV mainly changes the first-order error constant and regimes in which it substantially improves trajectory accuracy.
tldr: This paper introduces a family of scalar auxiliary variable (SAV) methods with pullback corrections for gradient flows, improving numerical stability and accuracy.
motivation: Standard SAV methods for gradient flows use a rank-one correction that may limit accuracy; the authors aim to decouple the number of scalar variables from the correction rank to achieve better performance.
method: The pullback-corrected SAV (PB-SAV) method uses a single scalar auxiliary variable but applies a low-rank positive semidefinite correction derived from an admissible component decomposition, implemented via Sherman-Morrison-Woodbury.
result: PB-SAV preserves modified-energy dissipation laws, yields a refinement identity with explicit weighted variance, and in finite dimensions the pullback correction equals the Gauss-Newton matrix of a least-squares energy representation.
conclusion: Numerical experiments on gradient flows, Allen-Cahn, and nonlocal Cahn-Hilliard models show that PB-SAV can substantially improve trajectory accuracy in certain regimes.

title: Dtpfi: A Stable Algorithm For Recovering Nonlinear Energy Potentials In Phase Field Systems
authors: Jun Lai Tianhao Ni
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18607v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work proposes a Dual Time Phase Field Inversion (DTPFI) method for recovering unknown potential functions in phase field models. The reconstruction is formulated as an optimization problem that minimizes the mismatch between model predictions and observed fields at the final measurement time. We prove the differentiability of the measured field with respect to the unknown potential and establish the local convexity of the regularized objective function, thereby ensuring the existence of a local optimal solution. For numerical implementation, automatic differentiation is employed to compute gradients, avoiding the expensive evaluation of analytic gradients. Extensive numerical experiments demonstrate that DTPFI accurately reconstructs both polynomial and logarithmic potentials and remains robust under measurement noise. The framework is further extended to inverse problems involving field dependent mobility and joint parameter identification in coupled Cahn-Hilliard-Allen-Cahn systems.
tldr: This paper presents a numerical algorithm for recovering unknown potential functions in phase field models, which is a topic in computational inverse problems and materials science.
motivation: Phase field models are used to simulate microstructure evolution, but determining the energy potential from experimental data is challenging. The authors aim to develop a stable and efficient inversion method.
method: The Dual Time Phase Field Inversion (DTPFI) method formulates the reconstruction as an optimization problem, uses automatic differentiation for gradient computation, and proves local convexity of the regularized objective.
result: Numerical experiments show accurate reconstruction of polynomial and logarithmic potentials, robustness to noise, and extension to field-dependent mobility and coupled systems.
conclusion: DTPFI is a stable and accurate algorithm for nonlinear potential recovery in phase field systems, with potential applications in materials science and inverse problems.

title: Generalization Of Selberg's $3/16$ Theorem For Geometrically Finite Thin Subgroups Of $\operatorname{SO}(n, 1)$
authors: Pratyush Sarkar
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18674v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a geometrically finite thin subgroup of an arithmetic lattice [MATH] and consider the congruence covers of [MATH]. In the breakthrough work of Bourgain-Gamburd-Sarnak, the expansion machinery was used to establish a uniform spectral gap in the setting [MATH] when the critical exponent satisfies [MATH]. The main applications are affine sieve for [MATH]-orbits and uniform resonance-free half-planes for the resolvent of the Laplacian. These results were generalized in subsequent works by Mohammadi-Oh, Oh-Winter, the author, and Edwards-Oh. Yet, the region [MATH] for [MATH] remains to be treated when there are cusps. The purpose of this paper is to fill in this gap in the literature. The difficulty lies in working with a countably infinite coding due to the presence of cusps. In particular, we incorporate new tools to prove the Zariski density and full trace field properties of the return trajectory subgroups.
tldr: This paper generalizes Selberg's 3/16 theorem to geometrically finite thin subgroups of SO(n,1), establishing a uniform spectral gap for congruence covers when the critical exponent is greater than n-2, even in the presence of cusps.
motivation: Previous work established a uniform spectral gap for thin subgroups of SO(n,1) when the critical exponent > n-2, but the case with cusps remained open. This paper fills that gap.
method: The author incorporates new tools to prove Zariski density and full trace field properties of return trajectory subgroups, enabling the analysis of countably infinite coding due to cusps.
result: A uniform spectral gap is established for geometrically finite thin subgroups of SO(n,1) with critical exponent > n-2, even when cusps are present.
conclusion: The result completes the generalization of Selberg's theorem to this setting, with applications to affine sieve and resonance-free half-planes.

title: Quasi-Monte Carlo Finite Element Approximation For Singularly Perturbed Convection-diffusion Problems With Random Velocity
authors: Seungchan Ko, Guanglian Li, Yi Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18678v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies the numerical approximation of a singularly perturbed convection-diffusion problem over a bounded polygonal domain in [MATH] ([MATH]), where the velocity field is modeled by a log-uniform random field, a setting typical in uncertainty quantification. We introduce a novel numerical framework for computing the expected value of the linear functionals of the solution. The approach combines a finite element discretization of the problem, a truncated Karhunen--Lo\`eve expansion to represent the stochastic velocity field, and a lattice-based quasi-Monte Carlo (QMC) method to estimate expectations over the parameter space. We provide a rigorous error analysis of the proposed scheme, establishing bounds on the mean squared error and demonstrating that the QMC method achieves a nearly linear optimal convergence rate, with a constant independent of the integration dimension. Furthermore, the convergence rate is shown to be independent of the singular perturbation parameter.
tldr: This paper develops a quasi-Monte Carlo finite element method for singularly perturbed convection-diffusion problems with random velocity fields, focusing on uncertainty quantification.
motivation: To efficiently compute expectations of linear functionals of solutions to convection-diffusion problems with random velocity, which arise in uncertainty quantification.
method: Combines finite element discretization, truncated Karhunen-Loève expansion for the random field, and lattice-based quasi-Monte Carlo integration.
result: Establishes rigorous error bounds showing nearly linear optimal convergence rate independent of integration dimension and singular perturbation parameter.
conclusion: The proposed framework achieves dimension-independent convergence for this class of stochastic PDEs.

title: Bayesian Prediction In Gamma Models: Admissibility And Infinitesimal Prediction
authors: Fumiyasu Komaki
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18700v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study estimation and prediction in the Gamma model [MATH], where the shape parameter [MATH] is known and the scale parameter [MATH] is unknown, under the Kullback--Leibler loss. For [MATH], all scale-invariant estimators of [MATH] have infinite risk, indicating a qualitative change in the estimation problem at the boundary [MATH]. Our main result is that the Bayesian predictive density based on the Jeffreys prior is admissible for all [MATH]. This resolves the admissibility problem for Bayesian predictive densities in Gamma models. As a related result, we also establish the admissibility of the corresponding Bayesian estimator for [MATH]. To prove the predictive admissibility result, we develop an infinitesimal prediction framework based on Gamma processes. This framework naturally leads to a Kullback--Leibler loss for L\'{e}vy densities and establishes a connection between predictive distributions and L\'{e}vy measures. Under the resulting loss, the Bayesian predictive L\'{e}vy density is shown to be the posterior mean L\'{e}vy density. Unlike the normal and Poisson models, infinitesimal prediction in the Gamma model does not reduce to parameter estimation. Instead, it reduces to the estimation of a L\'{e}vy density. We relate this phenomenon to mean mixture curvature and discuss it from an information-geometric viewpoint.
tldr: This paper studies Bayesian prediction in Gamma models under Kullback-Leibler loss, proving admissibility of the Jeffreys prior predictive density and developing an infinitesimal prediction framework.
motivation: The paper addresses a gap in admissibility results for Bayesian predictive densities in Gamma models, particularly at the boundary shape parameter value.
method: The authors develop an infinitesimal prediction framework based on Gamma processes, connecting predictive distributions to Lévy measures and using information geometry.
result: The Bayesian predictive density based on the Jeffreys prior is admissible for all shape parameters, and the corresponding estimator is also admissible.
conclusion: The work resolves the admissibility problem for Gamma models and highlights a qualitative difference from normal and Poisson models.

title: Fast Primal-dual Methods For Convex-concave Bilinear Saddle Point Problems: Continuous-time Dynamics And Discrete Algorithms
authors: Ya-Ping Fang Xin He
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18724v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies Nesterov accelerated methods for continuously differentiable convex-concave bilinear saddle point problems. For the continuous-time model, we analyze a second-order primal-dual dynamical system with vanishing damping [MATH], where [MATH]. Under the merely convex-concave setting, we prove convergence of the primal-dual trajectory to a saddle point. In the noncritical regime [MATH], we further obtain the improved rate [MATH] for the primal-dual gap and [MATH] for the velocity, and, under an additional Lipschitz gradient assumption, [MATH] for the stationarity residual. We then derive a structure-preserving finite-difference discretization, which leads to a fast primal-dual algorithm with Nesterov extrapolation. For a general accelerated parameter sequence [MATH] satisfying [MATH] with [MATH], we prove the [MATH] convergence rate for the primal-dual gap and convergence of the generated sequence. In the noncritical case [MATH], we further establish the improved rate [MATH] for the gap and [MATH] for the stationarity residual. These results provide continuous-discrete acceleration methods for bilinear saddle point problems in the merely convex-concave setting.
tldr: This paper develops fast primal-dual methods for convex-concave bilinear saddle point problems using continuous-time dynamics and discrete algorithms.
motivation: To accelerate convergence of algorithms for saddle point problems, which are important in optimization and machine learning.
method: Analyzes a second-order primal-dual dynamical system with vanishing damping and derives a structure-preserving finite-difference discretization leading to a Nesterov-accelerated algorithm.
result: Proves convergence rates for the primal-dual gap and stationarity residual under convex-concave and noncritical settings.
conclusion: Provides continuous and discrete acceleration methods for bilinear saddle point problems with improved convergence guarantees.

title: Norming Approximate Orthogonality In Normed Linear Spaces
authors: Saikat Roy
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18727v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce and study the notion of , a two-parameter generalization of Birkhoff--James orthogonality in normed linear spaces. For [MATH] with [MATH], we say [MATH] in [MATH] if there exists [MATH] with [MATH] and [MATH], simultaneously relaxing both the norming condition on [MATH] and the vanishing condition on [MATH]. It is proved that \[ x\nperp y \iff \|x+\lambda y\|\geq (1-\delta)\|x\|-{1-\delta}\|\lambda y\|~\qquad \forall ~~\lambda. \] This framework interpolates between two notions of approximate orthogonality in normed linear spaces due to Chmieli\'nski and Dragomir, and recovers three existing notions of orthogonality in extreme cases: exact Birkhoff--James orthogonality at [MATH], the approximate orthogonality of Chmieli\'nski at [MATH], and the approximate orthogonality of Dragomir at [MATH]. A two-parameter proximity result generalizing Chmlie\'nski's characterization of [MATH] is established. The forward and converse implications are governed by the distinct thresholds [MATH] and [MATH], which collapse to [MATH] of Chmieli\'nski precisely when [MATH], and the strictness of this gap is confirmed by counterexamples in [MATH]. A dual formulation of norming approximate orthogonality is established with a complete equivalence in the reflexive case. We apply our results to (vector-valued) continuous function spaces, which extends some earlier results and recovers few operator theoretical results with alternative proofs using measure theoretic techniques.
tldr: This paper introduces a two-parameter generalization of Birkhoff-James orthogonality in normed linear spaces, studying its properties and applications.
motivation: To unify and generalize existing notions of approximate orthogonality in functional analysis.
method: The authors define a new orthogonality relation with two parameters and prove equivalent characterizations, duality results, and applications to function spaces.
result: The framework interpolates between Chmieliński's and Dragomir's approximate orthogonalities and recovers exact Birkhoff-James orthogonality in limiting cases.
conclusion: The new notion provides a flexible tool for studying orthogonality in normed spaces, with potential extensions to operator theory.

title: Analyzing Changes In Optimal Variables In Linear Programming With Uncertain Parameters
authors: Baptiste Istace, Guillaume Derval, Bardhyl Miftari, Quentin Louveaux
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18830v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Linear problems often include many parameters that may be uncertain. Sensitivity analysis studies how these parameters impact optimal values. Instead of analyzing the objective function, we shift the focus to the optimal values of the variables. Three types of linear modifications are considered: on the cost vector, the right-hand side, and on the constraint matrix. Several theorems establish properties of these modifications, including conditions for continuity of optimal variable values, as well as local convexity and concavity properties.
tldr: This paper studies sensitivity analysis of optimal variable values in linear programming under parameter uncertainty.
motivation: Linear programming problems often involve uncertain parameters, and understanding how optimal variable values change with these parameters is important for robust optimization.
method: The authors consider three types of linear modifications (cost vector, right-hand side, constraint matrix) and prove theorems about continuity, local convexity, and concavity of optimal variable values.
result: Theorems establish conditions for continuity and local convexity/concavity of optimal variable values under parameter modifications.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for sensitivity analysis focused on optimal variables rather than the objective function.

title: Unconditional Primality Certificates For The Hexagonal 3-smooth Family P = 3m(m+1) + 1: Deterministic Pocklington Witnesses And Arithmetic Filters
authors: Hassane Bakkaoui
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18859v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the parametric subfamily p = 3m(m+1) + 1 with m = 2^a 3^b - 1, a,b in N*, a 3-smooth slice of the centred hexagonal numbers 3m^2 + 3m + 1 = (m+1)^3 - m^3, from the point of view of unconditional primality certification via the Pocklington-Lehmer criterion. The 3-smoothness of m+1 = 2^a 3^b yields, for every (a,b), a fully factored divisor F = 2^a 3^(b+1) of p-1 satisfying F > sqrt(p) unconditionally, reducing the certificate to two witnesses, for q = 2 and q = 3. Our main new contribution is a complete, deterministic characterisation of the two canonical witnesses. We prove that w_2 = 5 is a valid witness if and only if a - b = 1, 2 (mod 4), by quadratic reciprocity; and that w_3 = 7 is a valid witness if and only if m is not congruent to 2 (mod 7), by cubic reciprocity in Z[omega] using the explicit Eisenstein factorisation p = ((1+m) - m omega)((1+m) - m omega^2). These two results turn the heuristic "5 and 7 always work" (which is in fact false) into exact congruence conditions, and yield a deterministic witness-selection rule. Alongside, three elementary arithmetic filters (mod 6, a (-3) quadratic-residue sieve, and a mod-7 forbidden-class test) remove about 87% of candidates at negligible cost. As a demonstration, a multi-core implementation produced four unconditional certificates on consumer hardware, the largest a prime of 29998 decimal digits.
tldr: This paper presents deterministic primality certificates for a specific family of numbers using Pocklington's criterion and quadratic/cubic reciprocity.
motivation: To provide unconditional primality proofs for numbers of the form p = 3m(m+1)+1 with m+1 = 2^a 3^b, replacing heuristic witness selection with exact conditions.
method: Uses the Pocklington-Lehmer criterion with a fully factored divisor F > sqrt(p) from the 3-smooth structure, and characterizes witnesses via quadratic and cubic reciprocity laws.
result: Deterministic conditions for witnesses 5 and 7 are derived, and three arithmetic filters eliminate 87% of candidates; certificates for primes up to 29998 digits are demonstrated.
conclusion: The approach yields efficient unconditional primality certification for this family, with potential extension to other parametric forms.

title: Environment-Aware Resource Allocation For Pinching-Antenna-Assisted Edma-noma Systems
authors: Yaxuan Luo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18899v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Environment division multiple access (EDMA) exploits line-of-sight (LoS) availability, blockage diversity, and spatial isolation in the propagation environment to regulate inter-region interference, while non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) improves intra-region access efficiency through power-domain multiplexing and successive interference cancellation (SIC). This paper investigates heterogeneous environment-map-aware user matching and power allocation for pinching-antenna-assisted EDMA-NOMA systems. Based on large-scale path loss and an exponential LoS blockage model, an average LoS/NLoS effective large-scale channel gain is constructed, allowing the environment map to affect both desired service links and inter-region interference links. This avoids the overly optimistic assumption that environmental blockage only suppresses interference. A utility-based joint user-pairing and power-allocation algorithm (UBA-JPPA) is then proposed to jointly account for system throughput and the scheduled-user Jain fairness index under NOMA power constraints and an SIC-consistent rate definition. Simulation results show that, compared with the ablation baseline without a heterogeneous environment map, the proposed scheme provides consistent gains in sum rate, fairness, and the throughput--fairness operating region. Meanwhile, a strong EDMA-OMA benchmark remains competitive in some high-SNR regimes, indicating that the focus of this work is to verify the benefit of heterogeneous environment information for EDMA-NOMA resource allocation rather than to claim that NOMA universally outperforms OMA.
tldr: This paper proposes a resource allocation algorithm for pinching-antenna-assisted EDMA-NOMA systems using environment-aware user pairing and power allocation.
motivation: To improve spectral efficiency and fairness in wireless communication by exploiting environmental information (LoS blockage) to manage interference in EDMA-NOMA systems.
method: The authors construct an average LoS/NLoS effective large-scale channel gain model and propose a utility-based joint user-pairing and power-allocation algorithm (UBA-JPPA) that optimizes sum rate and fairness.
result: Simulations show consistent gains in sum rate and fairness compared to ablation baselines, though a strong EDMA-OMA benchmark remains competitive in high-SNR regimes.
conclusion: The work demonstrates the benefit of heterogeneous environment information for EDMA-NOMA resource allocation, but does not claim universal superiority over OMA.

title: Optimal Consumption And Retirement Time Under Shortfall Risk Measure
authors: Lijun Bo, Yijie Huang, Tingting Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18935v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies the optimal portfolio, consumption, and endogenous early retirement problem within a benchmark tracking framework by incorporating a new relative performance evaluation. In this framework, the investor maximizes expected lifetime consumption utility while managing the maximum wealth shortfall relative to a benchmark, with shortfall-management costs that may differ before and after retirement. Mathematically, the problem is a hybrid stochastic control problem involving both regular controls and an optimal stopping time, in which the running maximum process records the investor's largest benchmark shortfall. We introduce an auxiliary reflected state process and establish an equivalent hybrid stochastic control problem. By proving the convex duality theorem, we technically transform the original problem into a two-dimensional pure optimal stopping problem with state reflection. This enables us to characterize the geometric structure of the stopping set and derive the feedback-form optimal retirement boundary, as well as optimal portfolio and consumption policies. Analytical examples and numerical simulations reveal a two-stage structure with more conservative investment and more aggressive consumption after retirement. Driven by the retirement option, the expected largest shortfall risk follows a pronounced U-shaped pattern with respect to wealth. Shortfall management costs, labor income, and leisure preference significantly influence retirement timing, investment, and consumption.
tldr: This paper studies optimal consumption, portfolio, and retirement timing under a benchmark shortfall risk measure, using stochastic control and optimal stopping.
motivation: To incorporate relative performance evaluation and shortfall risk into optimal consumption and retirement decisions.
method: Formulates a hybrid stochastic control problem with regular controls and optimal stopping, transforms it via convex duality into a two-dimensional optimal stopping problem with reflection.
